skill.name: hypothesis-generation
skill.description: Generate evidence-based scientific hypotheses from observations, literature context, and research questions. Design tests, predictions, comparisons, and structured reports.
skill.summary: Build testable scientific hypotheses with predictions, experimental designs, and structured reporting.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, LaTeX macros, local file references, and public PubMed search examples. Two findings are confirmed as medium-risk external command guidance because the skill asks users to run a schematic-generation Python command and LaTeX compilation commands.

remediation.issue: Schematic generation uses a Bash command that invokes an external Python script.
remediation.suggestion: Make schematic generation optional, document the required script source, and avoid passing unsanitized user text to shell commands.

remediation.issue: Report compilation requires xelatex and bibtex external commands.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before compiling untrusted LaTeX and recommend sandboxed compilation with shell escape disabled.

remediation.issue: Literature search guidance may send sensitive research terms to public services.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to remove confidential, proprietary, or personally identifiable details before using PubMed or web search queries.

content.value_statement: Scientific ideas often fail when mechanisms, predictions, and tests are vague. This skill structures literature review, competing hypotheses, predictions, and experiment plans.
actual_capabilities: Turns observations or research questions into 3-5 competing scientific hypotheses.
Evaluates hypotheses against testability, falsifiability, parsimony, and explanatory power.
Suggests experimental designs, controls, measurements, and confound checks.
Creates predictions that help distinguish competing explanations.
Organizes findings into a concise report structure with appendices and citation guidance.
limitations: Does not prove that a hypothesis is true without expert review and empirical testing.
Requires clear user input about observations, constraints, domain, and acceptable methods.
Current citations may require external literature search tools.
Figure generation and LaTeX compilation depend on local tools that may not be installed.

use_cases.title: Plan a Thesis Study
use_cases.description: Turn an early research question into competing hypotheses, measurable predictions, and a feasible study plan.

use_cases.title: Compare Mechanistic Explanations
use_cases.description: Organize evidence for several mechanisms and identify experiments that can separate them.

use_cases.title: Prepare Grant Concepts
use_cases.description: Build a structured concept note with hypotheses, evidence gaps, predictions, and proposed tests.

prompt_templates.title: Start From an Observation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for turning one observation into initial hypotheses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three testable scientific hypotheses for this observation: [observation]. Include a short mechanism and one prediction for each hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Competing Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for ranking existing hypotheses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these hypotheses for [phenomenon]: [hypotheses]. Score testability, falsifiability, parsimony, explanatory power, and key weaknesses.

prompt_templates.title: Design Discriminating Experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: Design experiments that distinguish these competing hypotheses: [hypotheses]. Include measurements, controls, expected outcomes, confounds, and feasibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Full Hypothesis Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert prompt for a complete research deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured hypothesis report for [research question]. Include literature context, 3-5 hypotheses, predictions, critical comparisons, experiments, and appendix guidance.

output_examples.input: Observation: a treatment improves symptoms only in patients with high baseline inflammation.
output: Hypothesis 1: The treatment acts through an inflammation-dependent pathway.
Prediction: Patients with low baseline inflammation show a smaller response.
Test: Stratify participants by inflammatory markers and compare treatment effects.

output_examples.input: Research question: why does a material become brittle after repeated heat cycles?
output: Competing explanations include microcrack accumulation, phase transition, and impurity migration.
A useful test compares microscopy, diffraction, and mechanical testing after controlled cycle counts.
The strongest hypothesis should predict both timing and location of observed structural changes.

output_examples.input: Grant concept: identify mechanisms behind a crop stress-resistance trait.
output_examples.output: The skill can produce a report outline with candidate mechanisms, discriminating predictions, field and lab tests, controls, and evidence gaps.

best_practices: Provide the observation, domain, known constraints, and any preliminary evidence before asking for hypotheses.
Ask for competing explanations before selecting a favored hypothesis.
Review proposed experiments with a domain expert before using them in real studies.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one preferred answer before exploring alternative explanations.
Do not treat generated citations or mechanisms as verified without checking sources.
Do not use confidential research data in public literature search queries.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates competing hypotheses, mechanisms, predictions, experimental tests, quality assessments, and structured report guidance.

faq.question: Can it replace a scientist or reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It supports research planning, but expert review and empirical evidence remain required.

faq.question: Does it perform live literature searches automatically?
faq.answer: It provides search strategies and may use available search tools when the environment supports them.

faq.question: Which domains can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for broad scientific use, including biomedical, laboratory, field, computational, and interdisciplinary research.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the observation, research question, domain, known evidence, constraints, and methods that are available.

faq.question: Can it produce publication-ready reports?
faq.answer: It can structure detailed reports, but users must verify content, citations, formatting, and scientific claims.
